0.headline: Norwest Venture Partners and Kedaara Capital-backed Veritas Finance IPO gets SEBI nod
0.heading: Norwest Venture Partners and Kedaara Capital-backed Veritas Finance IPO gets SEBI nod
0.intro: Veritas Finance IPO | The professionally managed NBFC plans to raise Rs 900 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares, while existing shareholders will sell up to 1.28 crore equity shares through an offer for sale.
0.body:
Veritas Finance, a Chennai-based non-banking financial company (NBFC), has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to proceed with its initial public offering (IPO).

The company, backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Kedaara Capital, refiled its draft IPO papers with the capital markets regulator on July 29, 2026, with a revised offer structure.

According to SEBI's processing status of draft offer documents published on November 9, the regulator issued its observations on Veritas Finance's draft prospectus on October 19, 2026.

The issuance of observations allows the company to proceed with the IPO process and file its red herring prospectus (RHP) with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), disclosing details such as the IPO opening dates and final issue structure.

The professionally managed NBFC plans to raise Rs 900 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares, while existing shareholders will sell up to 1.28 crore equity shares through an offer for sale (OFS).

Investors Lok Capital Growth Fund and UK government-backed British International Investment plc, along with individuals D Arulmany, Growth Catalyst Partners LLC and Vidya Arulmany, will be among the selling shareholders in the OFS.

Earlier, Veritas Finance had filed its draft IPO papers in January 2025, aiming to raise up to Rs 2,800 crore through the public issue. Subsequently, SEBI approved the draft offer document in April 2025. However, the company did not proceed with its IPO plans at the time.

As part of the fresh issue, Veritas Finance may consider raising up to Rs 180 crore through a pre-IPO placement. If the company undertakes such a placement before filing the RHP with the RoC, the fresh issue size will be reduced accordingly.

The net proceeds from the fresh issue will be utilised to augment the company's capital base and meet future business requirements, including onward lending.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Norwest Venture Partners, with a 21.58 percent stake, is the largest shareholder in Veritas Finance, followed by Kedaara Capital Fund (15.08 percent), British International Investment (10.33 percent), and Lok Capital, founded by Rajiv Lall and Vishal Mehta, with a 9.48 percent stake.

Incorporated in 2015, Veritas Finance is a retail-focused NBFC primarily catering to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and self-employed individuals. It offers a range of financial products, including small business loans, housing loans, used commercial vehicle loans and working capital loans.

For the financial year ended March 2026, the company's net profit increased 12 percent year-on-year to Rs 330.4 crore, while net interest income (NII) rose 18 percent to Rs 1,133.5 crore, compared with the previous financial year.

The company's assets under management (AUM) increased 24.3 percent to Rs 9,134 crore in FY26 from Rs 7,348.6 crore in the previous year. Disbursements rose 16.4 percent to Rs 4,579.5 crore from Rs 3,933.1 crore during the same period.

Veritas Finance considers listed companies such as Five-Star Business Finance, SBFC Finance, Aavas Financiers, Aptus Value Housing Finance India and Sundaram Finance among its comparable peers.

ICICI Securities, IIFL Capital Services, JM Financial and SBI Capital Markets are the merchant bankers managing the Veritas Finance IPO.

1.headline: MakeMyTrip's India arm gets SEBI nod to float IPO
1.heading: MakeMyTrip's India arm gets SEBI nod to float IPO
1.intro: MakeMyTrip (India) Ltd (MMT India) had filed draft papers with Sebi in July through the confidential route
1.body:
Nasdaq-listed travel booking platform MakeMyTrip's India subsidiary has received SEBI's approval to launch an initial public offering (IPO), according to an update available on the market regulator's website on Monday.

MakeMyTrip (India) Ltd (MMT India) had filed draft papers with Sebi in July through the confidential route. After examining the draft documents, the regulator issued its final observations on November 6.

SEBI's observations mark an important step in the IPO process, allowing the company to proceed with preparations for its public issues, subject to applicable regulatory requirements.

The proposed IPO is expected to comprise a sale of equity shares in MMT India by its parent MakeMyTrip and its wholly-owned subsidiary, ibibo Group Holdings (Singapore) Pte Ltd, the Gurugram-headquartered company said in a regulatory filing with Nasdaq.

Following the completion of the proposed IPO, MMT India will continue to remain a subsidiary of MakeMyTrip, with its financial results continuing to be consolidated with those of the parent company, it had said.

"MakeMyTrip expects the proposed initial public offering and listing of MMT India to enhance its brand visibility and support MMT India's ability to incentivise and promote talent in a competitive technology recruitment landscape," the filing stated.

The net proceeds received by MakeMyTrip and ibibo Group Holdings from the sale of shares in MMT India are expected to strengthen the parent's cash position.

The proceeds will be utilised for long-term growth, strategic inorganic initiatives and repurchases of different classes of securities, including convertible securities, by MakeMyTrip, the filing stated.

2.headline: Antala Industries shares to list on November 11; check latest GMP, expected listing price
2.heading: Antala Industries shares to list on November 11; check latest GMP, expected listing price
2.intro: Antala Industries shares are set to debut on the stock market on November 11, after a public issue that drew strong investor demand, with the initial public offering (IPO) subscribed 12.2 times on the final day of bidding.
2.body:
Antala Industries shares are set to make their stock market debut on November 11, following a public issue that attracted strong investor demand, with the initial public offering (IPO) subscribed 12.2 times on the final day of bidding.

The Rs 22.98-crore Antala Industries IPO received bids for 4.25 crore shares against 34.82 lakh shares on offer, according to exchange data. The issue was open for subscription from October 29 to November 5.

Read Also: Vedant Poly Fabs shares make flat debut on NSE Emerge, list at issue price of Rs 94

The Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIB) category led the demand, with the portion reserved for institutional investors subscribed 66.72 times. The non-institutional investors (NII) category was subscribed 37.38 times, while the retail individual investors' portion received bids 5.22 times the shares on offer.

The grey market premium (GMP) of Antala Industries IPO stood at Rs 0 on the morning of November 9, according to IPOWatch. This indicates that the shares were trading at par with their upper issue price of Rs 66 in the unofficial market.

Based on the latest GMP, the estimated listing price of Antala Industries shares is Rs 66, indicating a flat market debut.

However, the grey market premium is an unofficial indicator and does not guarantee the actual listing price. It can change before the shares make their stock market debut.

Check IPO News Here

Antala Industries launched its Rs 22.98-crore SME IPO with a price band of Rs 62-66 per share.

The basis of allotment was finalised on November 6, while refunds and credit of shares to demat accounts are scheduled for November 9. The shares are scheduled to list on the BSE SME platform on November 11.

The company plans to utilise the IPO proceeds towards meeting its working capital requirements, purchasing machinery and general corporate purposes.
